newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina, Japan vow to increase trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Japan vow to increase trade ties.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem and Japan's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazuo Ogura vowed Friday to increase trade ties between their nations.

Ogura, who is in Buenos Aires seeking closer links with Mercosur custom union members Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, said a center for information on Argentina will soon be opened in Tokyo to help those interested in doing business with the South American country.

At a news conference after talks with Menem, Ogura praised the "magnitude of economic reform in Argentina and president Menem's leadership, which have generated the confidence of international investors, as the presence of Toyota in this country testifies."
Toyota Motor Corp 7203 is buidling a plant in Argentina and hopes to start producing Hilux pickup trucks at the end of 1996 at an annual rate of 20,000.
Argentina last year sold Japan $457 million worth of goods, mostly processed and unprocessed food, and it imported capital goods, cars and other industrial products for a total $711 million.
Ogura will fly on to Brazil on Sunday to attend a Mercosur meeting in Sao Paulo, Brazil's industrial heartland.

Mercosur, established in 1995, recently signed a free trade agreement with Chile and is holding free trade talks with a number of countries and groups, including the European Union and the Andean Group of five Latin American nations.
"Japan visualizes Mercosur as a region which is growing and will continue to grow a lot," Argentina's top Mercosur official Jorge Campbell told reporters after talks with Ogura.
